lines.en: I circle the blue banner on patrol.
I keep step with the knights.
Light steps under my blue tabard.
I move to a loophole in the wall.
I walk the edge of the rampart.
I round the tents to my next post.
My boots kick up a layer of dust.
I back three paces for a clear shot.
I take the ladder up to the lookout.
I pass the blue soldiers by.
I step down the haystack slope.
The column moves; I follow.
I set the blue banner straight.
My arrow stays nocked.
I lean on the wall and listen for horns.
I count the figures across the field.
A bowstring needs constant checking.
The wind on the lookout is cold.
I stretch my arms out.
The banner flaps overhead.
I stare across the moat.
Just keep blades away from me.

lines.zh: 我在蓝旗下面问你是谁
lines.en: I ask who you are under the blue flag.
Bow lowered, courtesy first.

lines.zh: 你穿的不是我们的颜色
lines.en: You wear none of our colours.
My eyes are on your weapon.
Stop, this is the blue camp.

lines.zh: 你不会是红方派来的吧
lines.en: You are not with the reds, are you?
I look over your boots.
Come closer and I will question you.
My fingers rest on the string.
Is anyone with you?

lines.zh: 我抬起下巴示意你站住
lines.en: I lift my chin for you to stop.
Look at me when you speak.
My quiver is torn open.
I bite down and stay silent.
Blood seeps through my sleeve.
I crouch and press the wound.
There is a new hole in my blue.
The bowstring cut my hand.
My shoulder will not lift.
I lean on the boards and pant.
My helmet is full of sweat.
I fall back under the banner.
That quiver is yours?
My eyes follow the fletching.
Good arrows are what we lack.
That head is honed with care.
I reach out and touch that arrow.
Two skins of wine for it.
Your bow is shorter than mine.
I swallow, eyeing the arrows.
Where did you get such goods?
I hug the quiver and hold on.
Do not bump me, I am aiming.
My helmet rings from the knock.
I step back to make way.
You stepped on my tabard.
The bump scatters my arrows.
My blue tabard is askew.
I catch the wall to stay upright.
Why shove, there is room ahead.
I frown and fix my belt.
Two archers colliding makes a mess.
She ties the blue banner for me.
We guard the same stretch of wall.
She lines up my arrows neatly.
I teach her to read the wind.
Side by side we watch the signal smoke.
She laughs at the shot I missed.
I lend her my bow to try.
Two of us crowd one battlement.
I remember where she stands.

lines.zh: 她的蓝袍和我的褪成一个色
lines.en: Her blue has faded to match mine.
I drop the arrow into my blue bag.
I pick up a brass buckle.
I pick up a fallen bow tip.
I gather the scattered arrows.
I pick up a foe's short blade.
I tuck it into my quiver.
I stoop for the broken flagstaff.
I log whatever I find.
I pick up one good arrow.
I fit the feather back on the nock.
The signals changed; attack.
I spot the reds closing in.
I shout a warning.
I draw the string back.
They are over the low wall.
I fix on the leader.
In range, ready to loose.
I hold my breath.
At least five charging in.
Let them taste my arrows.
The reds' banner corner shows.
I shout down from the wall.
The one with the axe leads them.
I pull him into my range.
I track him along the merlon.
He hides; I wait him out.
I shift to the next loophole.
My aim does not drift.
He goes left; I follow left.
On three I loose.
The string brushes my cheek.
He raises a shield; I aim low.
I will not waste an arrow.
He has nowhere to run.
He creeps along the wall's foot.
I nudge the bow slightly right.
I wait for him to cross the ditch.
He has stopped to look around.
I use the pause to aim.
He does not know I am up here.

lines.zh: 这个角度正好穿过城垛
lines.en: This angle clears the merlons.
My arrow bites through his pauldron.
I loose, and the arrow flies.
The first arrow makes him duck.
The second sticks in his shield.
When he closes, I back off.
I parry his blade with my bow.
I shoot at his ankle.
That arrow grazed his neck.
I loosed two arrows in a row.
He is down; I pick a new target.
The fletching still trembles.
I swing the blue banner at him.
He topples off the ladder.
I hit the hand holding the torch.
A blue-fletched arrow stands in his shoulder.
I loose a close shot along the wall.
He crashes into the palisade.
I add one more shaft for good.
The blue flag opens; I take my place.
I walk into camp with a full quiver.
The lookout gains a blue archer.
I appear from behind the tent.
I garrison in with the blue knights.
First I string my bow.
My blue tabard ripples in the wind.
I pick a good stretch of wall.
I take position at the horn call.
I look up at the blue banner.
This camp is new to me.
I plant my feet on the merlon.
A fire arrow caught my sleeve.
I dropped off the lookout.
Moat water pours into my mouth.
The blast shreds the palisade.
An enemy arrow found me.
Spell light burns into my armour seams.
I am too starved to draw.
Lightning scorched the blue flag.
Banner and I both fall away.
